statement_record.book: X.7 Theorem 1: a functor T : M → A has a colimit iff it has a left Kan extension along the unique K1 : M → 1, and then Colim T is the value of Lan_{K1} T at the object of 1; dually, right Kan extensions along K1 give limits.
statement_record.intree: Kan_Limit : Lim ≅ Ran (Erase J) F ttt, given `{Limit F} and `{RightKan (Erase J) C}.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: (a) only the DUAL half is proven — limit ≅ Ran along Erase; the primary colimit = Lan-along-K1 direction has no in-tree theorem (no Kan_Colimit; grep 'Kan.*Colim|colim.*Kan' -> essay mentions only). (b) The book's existence-biconditional and identity of universal properties ('has a colimit iff has a Kan extension') is reduced to an object isomorphism assuming BOTH a Limit and the GLOBAL RightKan (adjoint) already exist; existence-transfer is not derived. (c) It uses the global RightKan class (the full adjoint Induced ⊣ Ran), not the local Kan extension of the single functor F.
